description:
Surgical micro-gripper references and separate next-version exploration. Jake is happy with current smaller-gear version and ready to print it; preserve v326_generalist_small_drive Base25/Gripper29 as current print candidate unchanged (user approval to try printing is not measured fit/strength certification). Wants another version inspired by surgical grippers, starting with images/CAD to inspect industry approaches to extremely fine motion. References need not be open source; clearly distinguish viewable reference from licensed reusable/manufacturable CAD.

Initial sourced shortlist: MMI Symani NanoWrist micro/supermicro instruments, manufacturer images and motion scaling/tremor reduction https://www.mmimicro.com/symani/how-it-works/ ; da Vinci Black Diamond Micro Forceps and wristed graspers, Intuitive instrument catalogue https://www.intuitive.com/en-us/-/media/ISI/Intuitive/Pdf/da-vinci-sp-instruments-accessories-catalog.pdf and https://www.intuitive.com/en-gb/products-and-services/da-vinci/instruments ; publicly downloadable dVRK Large Needle Driver420006 high/low-res OBJ+MTL meshes https://github.com/jhu-dvrk/instrument-cad derived from Intuitive-provided models, no clear standard open hardware license in root listing, not manufacturing drawings. Author overview https://jackzhy96.github.io/build/01-instrument-cad/ . Simple precision tweezer reference: Dumont5 https://finescience.com/dumont-5-forceps/11251-10 tips0.08x0.04mm, explicitly laboratory/research product not human-use instrument.

Create sourced visual reference gallery with clickable originals, mechanism closeups and available downloadable model links, preferably reachable via existing hosted preview. Explain jaw-tip geometry, tiny hinge/tendon/rod transmission, remote actuation, stiffness/backlash/preload and motion scaling; do not confuse tiny tips with system positioning accuracy. Show distinction between actual surgical grasper and gripper holding surgical instruments. Propose separate minimal-part fine-motion concept appropriate to our hand-held gripper constraints, preserving original-tip contact, motor centered/above finger plane, low in-plane support and actual servo mounting. Do not retrofit or overwrite accepted print version. If CAD concept made, new counters only for changed parts and clearly label exploratory. No unsupported clinical suitability or micron accuracy claims; references for robot assembly/fine manipulation, not authorization to build surgical device.

results.identified_issue: The request prioritizes sourced image/CAD inspection before a separate next-version exploration while preserving v326 Base 25/Gripper 29. Delivered a static reference gallery served by the existing publisher and linked from Live Preview. No part geometry, VERSIONS.txt, catalogue generation rules or version counters changed. Xi/X catalogue p6 identifies Black Diamond Micro Forceps 470033; SP catalogue does not. dVRK Large Needle Driver 420006 is a different instrument. GitHub tree pinned to 96f9819db660e85879f157c58e4ec79744ae2c59 has OBJ/MTL meshes but no standard hardware license in root/tool README. Manufacturer images are externally embedded with original links; no third-party CAD was incorporated into our design. Engineering mechanisms and generic sketches are labeled interpretation. Proposed later branch replaces the upper drive with an integral drum/crank, short cable and opening spring while retaining lower counter-gears, original finger band, sleeves and actual HLS3606M-C001 plate/case mounting. Illustrative 6/18 radius ratio is a local tangent approximation, not a verified finite-stroke mechanism; cable guide, spring loads, servo travel and residual lower-gear backlash remain unresolved. Diff check confirms v326 unchanged. Publisher --no-build succeeded; 18 model/publisher tests passed. Chrome desktop and CDP mobile emulation at390px checked all3 images loaded and scrollWidth==innerWidth==390. No physical phone, CAD feasibility, actuator motion or clinical suitability verified. Existing unrelated Generated/GitInfo.swift changes left untouched.
results.summary: Added surgical micro-gripper references and a separate fine-motion proposal.
results.detailed_description:
Live Preview now has a “Surgical micro-gripper references” link: NanoWrist closeups, da Vinci catalogues, downloadable dVRK meshes, and Dumont tweezers. Each distinguishes reference material from reusable manufacturing CAD; dVRK reuse rights remain unclear. External images need internet access.

The separate cable-and-spring proposal retains our original tips, lower jaw gears and real overhead servo mounting. It is a sketch, not printable CAD; routing, backlash and force need validation. Base 25 / Gripper 29 is unchanged. Review the gallery and concept before the next CAD version. Desktop and 390-pixel mobile rendering passed, along with 18 gallery/publisher tests; no phone or hardware test was performed.

results.notes: Additional Jake feedback: he recalls a FOUR-SCREW motor attachment from assembling SO-101 hands. Double-check exact hardware before next version, and reduce number of bolts where feasible. Current accepted Base25 uses HLS3606M-C001 from Aero Hand, whereas SO-101 uses STS3215; explicitly compare those actual output horn/plate and case-mount interfaces rather than transplanting one screw pattern to the other. Verify sourced drawings/STEP/part revision, spline plate holes vs center retaining screw vs motor case screws, thread sizes/PCD/depth/access. Explain discrepancy plainly with closeup annotated exploded views. Count actual bolts before/after; simplify adapters/consolidate fasteners only with viable load path, axial capture, accessible assembly and anti-loosening strategy, not by hiding screws. User asks verification and possible simplification, not an implicit motor swap. Preserve accepted Base25/Gripper29 print candidate; if verification reveals a real fit error, report it clearly before he prints and make corrected geometry a separate version. Carry into surgical-reference next-version exploration without unnecessary surgical wrist complexity. /Users/jakeschantz/HelpingHands
